_en.title: Tomato Parsley Salad
_en.intro:
20230710 #breakfastdiary 782, 22°C/cloudy, 21min/workout(Y)
Making breakfast every day means I always need a little leafy green on hand, and parsley, perilla leaves, and (among mints) spearmint keep especially well compared to other greens — they're incredibly handy.
With rain forecast all week, I feel like I need to brace both body and mind.
1. Wash the large and small tomatoes.
2. Slice the large tomato and lay it on the plate as a base; cut the small tomatoes into sixths (quartering made them a bit too big) and scatter on top. Sprinkle with chopped parsley.
3. Drizzle evenly with vinaigrette.
#breakfast #recipe #miraclemorning #tomato, parsley

_en.title: Baked Potato with Cheddar and Bacon
_en.intro:
20230709 #breakfastdiary 781, 24°C/cloudy
1. Wash the potatoes well, score them lengthwise with vertical cuts, and let them sit in water for a bit.
2. Brush the potatoes with melted butter and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes.
3. Chop bacon finely and pan-fry it; mince the parsley.
4. Take the potatoes out of the oven, cut cheddar cheese into quarters, and tuck the pieces into the slits. Bake at 180°C for about 10 minutes, until the cheese melts.
5. Plate the potatoes and top with Greek yogurt and the bacon and parsley from step 3.

_en.title: Leek Gratin in Cream Sauce
_en.intro:
20230708 #breakfastdiary 780, 25°C/cloudy
1. Mix 2T cream soup, 2T milk, 1/2T grated garlic, 2T parmesan cheese, 1/2T wholegrain mustard, and herbs to make the sauce. (Adjust the thickness by adding more milk.)
2. Cut the leeks, arrange them neatly, pour the sauce over, and bake at 180°C for 30 minutes.
3. Take it out of the oven, sprinkle with parmesan cheese, and bake again at 200°C for 20 minutes.
1. For the roux: melt butter in a pan and stir in flour in two additions, using a 1:1 butter-to-flour ratio.
2. The roux-to-milk ratio is 1:7 — pour the milk into the roux and stir to loosen it. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

_en.title: Grilled Eggplant with Greek Yogurt
_en.intro:
20230707 #breakfastdiary 797, 23°C/mostly cloudy, 21min/workout(Y)
You should have seen the vivid purple that flashes for just a moment when eggplant is cooked through, right before it turns reddish-brown.
1. Wash the eggplant well, halve it, and cook in a hot pan with olive oil. It softens quickly, so start with the cut side down.
2. Mix half a shallot, 3T olive oil, 1T wine vinegar, and 1/2T wholegrain mustard to make the dressing.
3. Plate the eggplant, spoon over the dressing, and finish with Greek yogurt, red pepper flakes, and parsley.

_en.title: Roasted Carrots with Parmesan
_en.intro:
20230706 #breakfastdiary 796, 24°C/mostly clear
The smell of parmesan cheese (grated) roasting in the oven is pretty irresistible.
1. Wash the carrots, peel them, and cut into bite-size pieces.
2. Make a sauce with olive oil, minced parsley, salt, pepper, paprika powder, and red pepper flakes.
3. Toss the carrots in the sauce, roll them in parmesan cheese, and roast at 220°C for 20 minutes.

_en.title: Cold Dumplings with Vinegar-Soy Dressing
_en.intro:
20230705 #breakfastdiary 795, 21°C/cloudy
"I've never once told anyone I 'failed.' It was simply a mistake. These days, young people use that frightening word — 'failure' — far too often. When we resist the word 'failure,' we become able to enjoy our mistakes and our pain."
(Kim Chang-il, terminal business owner, one of the world's top 100 collectors, on the artist C-Kim's dream)
Failure isn't something to fear (doesn't Finland even have a Day for Failure?), but it doesn't need to be a constant refrain either.
1. Blanch store-bought water dumplings in boiling water, then plate them.
2. Mix 3T water, 1T soy sauce, 1T vinegar, 1T sugar, and a splash of sesame oil for the dressing, and pour over the dumplings. Finish with chopped scallion.

title: 라따뚜이
intro:

_en.title: Ratatouille
_en.intro:
20230704 #breakfastdiary 794, 25°C/cloudy, 21min/workout(Y)
In Korean it's 'ratatouille,' but read the way the French actually pronounce it, it's more like 'ha-ta-too-ee.'
1. Wash the eggplant, zucchini, and tomato well, and slice them into rounds.
2. Pour tomato sauce into an oven-safe pot, then layer in the eggplant, zucchini, and tomato.
3. Drizzle with olive oil, add plenty of salt and pepper, and bake at 180°C for 15 minutes — it came out a little underdone, so 30 minutes would probably be better.
Forgot the parmesan cheese, but anyway, a simple #ratatouille for a busy morning.

_en.title: Braised Eggplant Rice Bowl
_en.intro:
20230702 #breakfastdiary 792, 25°C/cloudy
1. Wash the eggplant, peel it, and steam it.
2. Make a sauce with 1T oyster sauce, 3T soy sauce, and 1T honey.
3. Put the steamed eggplant in a pan, pour over the sauce, and simmer down.
4. Top a bowl of rice with the eggplant, an egg yolk, chopped scallion, sesame seeds, and sesame oil.
A soft, moist eggplant rice bowl even my mother, who has trouble chewing, can enjoy.

_en.title: Tortilla Pizza
_en.intro:
20230701 #breakfastdiary 791, 25°C/mostly clear
1. Lay a tortilla in a pan, add mozzarella cheese, and cover with a lid until the cheese melts.
2. While the cheese melts, mix 3T mayonnaise, 2T honey, 1T lemon juice, and plenty of pepper to make a dressing.
3. Plate the tortilla and drizzle on the dressing.
4. Top with well-washed spinach and sautéed ham (bacon would probably suit it even better). Finish with parmesan cheese.
A keystone that serves no structural purpose was carved as decoration above a square window, and people happily paid a higher price for a house whose ornamentation gave off an air of old-world elegance. Form and function had drifted apart, but that gap was smoothed over by the familiarity we call taste.
(Lim Woo-jin, The Origin of Ornament)
The keystone, which once bore the weight at the center of an arch, has somewhere along the way lost its original function and kept only its form. How many things around us are just like that?

_en.title: Spinach Tomato Cheese Wrap
_en.intro:
20230630 #breakfastdiary 790, 22°C/cloudy, 20min/workout(Y)
Are you doing okay —
even though we meet every day,
that's still what I most want to know.
'Yeah,' I answer with a nod,
and even that is the heaviest single syllable.
(Kim So-yeon, No Return 5)
1. Melt a knob of butter in a pan and blanch the spinach.
2. Add tomato, cheese, and two beaten eggs, then gently cover with a tortilla and flip after 1–2 minutes.
3. After another 1–2 minutes, take the tortilla out of the pan, let it cool slightly, roll it up like a gimbap, and cut it in half.
I'll call this one a #spinachtomatocheesewrap — plump, since I packed in so many fillings.

_en.title: Carrot Salad
_en.intro:
20230619 #breakfastdiary 787, 25°C/mostly clear, 21min/workout(Y)
Boiled carrots are a real love-it-or-hate-it thing. What do boiled carrots mean to you?
1. Wash the carrots, peel them, and boil for about 10 minutes.
2. Drain and place in a bowl, then mix in butter, salt, pepper, and parsley.

title: 톳면
intro:
20230613, #조식다이어리 782, 18도/대체로흐림, 21분/운동(Y)
톳면(혹은 톳국수)에 시즈닝한 새우를 곁들인 톳면 샐러드
1. 톳을 넣어 만든 #톳면 을 물에 씻어 채에 받혀둔다. 
2. 달군 팬에 올리브오일, 소금소금, 후추후추, 허브허브 새우를 굽는다. 
3. 접시에 톳면과 새우를 담고 비네그레트 드레싱, 다진 파슬리
궁극에 이르러 사람들이 당신에 대해 기억하는 것, 
얼마나 바빴는지, 
얼마나 일했는지, 
명품을 몇 개나 가졌는지, 
보다는
어떤 감정을 느끼게 만들었는지,
약속을 지켰는지, 
신뢰할 수 있는지, 
(출처: 트위터 economakase)
다만 현실에선 위 두 그룹이 연동된다. 
(문제에 직면했을 때 이를 헤쳐나갈) 의사결정 방법이라고 알려진, 
1. 일어날 수 있는 최악의 상황은 무엇인지, 2. 일어날 가능성은 얼마나 되는지, 3. 그것을 감당할 수 있는지에 대해 고민하기 전에 지금 당면한 문제의 본질에 대해서 생각하는 게 먼저 아닌가 싶다. 
2. 대부분 최악의 문제는 최악이 아닌 경우가 많다.

_en.title: Hijiki Noodle Salad with Shrimp
_en.intro:
20230613 #breakfastdiary 782, 18°C/mostly cloudy, 21min/workout(Y)
A hijiki noodle salad, tot-myeon (a.k.a. tot noodles) topped with seasoned shrimp.
1. Rinse the #TotMyeon (noodles made with hijiki seaweed) and drain well.
2. Sear the shrimp in a hot pan with olive oil, a good pinch of salt, pepper, and herbs.
3. Plate the noodles and shrimp together, finish with vinaigrette and chopped parsley.
In the end, what people remember about you
isn't how busy you were,
how hard you worked,
or how many luxury items you owned,
but how you made them feel,
whether you kept your word,
whether you could be trusted.
(source: Twitter, economakase)
Except in reality, the two groups above tend to go hand in hand.
Before running through the so-called decision-making method for facing a problem —
1. what's the worst that could happen, 2. how likely is that, 3. could you handle it — I think it's worth first considering the nature of the problem actually in front of you.
2. Most of the time, the worst-case problem turns out not to be so bad after all.

_en.intro:

_en.intro:
20230610 #breakfastdiary 779, 19°C/cloudy
Now that June's here, Korean squash (joseon hobak) has started catching my eye. #KoreanSquashSoftTofuSalad
1. Wash the squash, cut off the top, scoop out the insides, then steam it for 10 minutes in a pot with a shallow pool of water.

3. Toast black sesame seeds and sprinkle them over the tofu. (Not sure it belongs, but I add mint too.)
This is a recipe from #MyLocalFoodSalad.

title: 라임 라임우동 누벨바그
intro:
20230608, #조식다이어리 777, 18도/흐림, 21분/운동(Y)

라임의 매력은 무엇보다 쌉싸름한 끝맛, 그건 산전 수전 공중전 겪은 어른들만 아는 맛이다. 
(육수)
1. 물 1리터에 다시마 2장, 표고 2개 넣고 끓인다. 물이 끓으면 다시마를 건져내고 가쯔오부시를 넣은 뒤 약불에 15분 끓인다. 채에 걸러 육수를 준비한다.

*육수를 미리 만들어 두면 바쁜 아침에도 간편하게 먹을 수 있다. (5분 컷)

_en.title: Lime Udon
_en.intro:
20230608 #breakfastdiary 777, 18°C/cloudy, 21min/workout(Y)
Lime udon — something I make once summer rolls around, and each year the taste gets a little better (proud of that).
The real charm of lime is that bittersweet finish, a flavor only grown-ups who've been through the wringer really understand.
(Broth)
1. Bring 1 liter of water to a boil with 2 sheets of dried kelp and 2 dried shiitake mushrooms. Once boiling, remove the kelp, add bonito flakes, and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes. Strain to prepare the broth.
2. Mix in 2 parts tsuyu, 2 parts mirin, and 1 part sugar. (Seasoning is kept light rather than strong.)
*Making the broth ahead of time means an easy meal even on a busy morning. (5-minute cut)
(Noodles)
1. Boil store-bought udon noodles for 2 minutes, then rinse in cold water (ice would be nice, but this works too) for extra chewy texture.
2. Place the noodles in a bowl, pour over the broth, and top with sliced lime.

_en.title: Banana Overnight Oats
_en.intro:
20230607 #breakfastdiary 776, 17°C/cloudy
Just a little effort the night before can make a busy morning feel abundant — overnight oats, left to sit overnight.
Layer in order: 1 mashed banana, 2 parts chia seeds, 2 parts oats, 1 small container of yogurt, and sliced banana, then sprinkle with cinnamon and chill in the fridge overnight.
Before agonizing over what the worst outcome (of this decision) could be, how likely it is, and whether you could handle it —
let's think first about the real nature of the problem in front of us.

title: 유니버설디자인 배리어프리 토마토부라타치즈샐러드
intro:
20230530, #조식다이어리 775, 19도/대체로흐림
몇 달 전 시립미술관, 드문드문 두 벌의 작품 해설이 붙어 있었고 좀 더 간결하고 짧은 해설 아래 이런 설명이 붙어 있었다. 
이 설명은 쉬운 정보로 만들었습니다. 
작품 해설이란 것이 늘 난해했기 때문에 이런 시도가 매우 반가웠는데, 최근에 그 출처(?)를 알게 됐다. #유니버설디자인 #배리어프리 가 물리적인 한계에 갇혀 있을 필요는 없지 않겠는가? 쉬운 정보를 제공하는 회사, 소소한 소통 @sosocommunication 웹 사이트의 내용을 덧붙인다. 
소소한소통은 모두를 위한 쉬운 정보를 제공합니다.
‘쉬운 정보’는 발달장애인, 외국인, 학습장애 어린이, 어르신 등 말과 글을 이해하기 어려운 이들에게도 필요하지만, 우리 모두에게 편한 정보입니다. 일상의 소소한 순간까지 소통의 어려움이 없는 삶 ‘소소한소통’이 함께 합니다.
오늘 조식은 방울토마토, 부라타치즈, 민트에 비네그레트 드레싱을 얹은 눈에 보이는 그대로 쉽고, 솔직한 #토마토부라타치즈샐러드

_en.title: Tomato Burrata Salad
_en.intro:
20230530 #breakfastdiary 775, 19°C/mostly cloudy
A few months ago at the city art museum, here and there I noticed two versions of the wall text for certain works — and under the shorter, simpler version was this note:
This description was written in easy-to-understand language.
Exhibit descriptions have always felt needlessly dense to me, so I was genuinely glad to see this effort, and I recently found out where it came from. Why should #UniversalDesign and #BarrierFree be limited to physical constraints? I'm adding some content from the website of Soso Communication (@sosocommunication), a company that provides easy-to-understand information.
Soso Communication provides easy information for everyone.
'Easy information' is essential for people with developmental disabilities, foreign residents, children with learning disabilities, and older adults — anyone who finds words and text hard to follow — but really, it makes life easier for all of us. Soso Communication is here for a life free of communication barriers, down to the small, everyday moments.
Today's breakfast is cherry tomatoes, burrata, and mint with a vinaigrette — a #TomatoBurrataSalad that's exactly as simple and honest as it looks.

title: 살구토스트 살구
intro:
20230529, #조식다이어리 774, 24도/비, 21분/운동(Y) 
살구를 설탕 넣고 데쳤더니 세상에서 제일 예쁜 색이 됐다. 
1. 살구를 깨끗하게 씻어 네 등분한 뒤 설탕, 레몬1/2개를 짜서 넣고 중불에 데친다. (설탕은 살구 분량의 1/5 정도, 하지만 적당히 넣어도 상관없다.) 완성 후 냉장고에 넣어둔다. 
2. 달군 팬에 올리브오일 두른 빵을 굽고 부라타치즈, 딜을 얹는다. 
3. 1의 살구 콩포트를 얹고 민트로 장식한다.

_en.title: Apricot Toast
_en.intro:
20230529 #breakfastdiary 774, 24°C/rain, 21min/workout(Y)
Poaching apricots with sugar gave them the prettiest color I've ever seen.
1. Wash the apricots well, cut into quarters, then poach over medium heat with sugar and the juice of half a lemon. (Use sugar at about 1/5 the weight of the apricots, though you can adjust to taste.) Once done, chill in the fridge.
2. Sear bread in a hot pan with olive oil, then top with burrata and dill.
3. Spoon the apricot compote from step 1 on top and finish with mint.

title: 계란찜 푸딩같은계란찜
intro:
20230528, #조식다이어리 773, 19도/비, 21분/운동(U) 
이대로 하면 분명히 푸딩 같은 계란찜이 된다고 했는데 가장자리는 그냥 계란찜이 됐다. 레시피 대로 한다고 그대로 되진 않는다. 조식(인생)엔 답이 없다. 
1. 계란 4개 잘 풀어서 소금 한 꼬집 넣고 물 200ml 부어 섞은 뒤 채에 거른다. 
2. 그릇에 담고 거품을 걷어낸 뒤 약불에서 15분, 불 끄고 5분 가량 뜸을 들인다. 
3. 굴소스, 올리고당 각 1, 간장, 참기름 각 1/2 넣어 드레싱을 만들어 계란찜 위에 붓는다.

_en.title: Almost-Pudding Steamed Egg
_en.intro:
20230528 #breakfastdiary 773, 19°C/rain, 21min/workout(U)
The recipe promised this would turn out just like a pudding-like steamed egg, but the edges ended up as plain old steamed egg. Following a recipe to the letter doesn't guarantee the same result. There's no single right answer in breakfast — or in life.
1. Beat 4 eggs well, add a pinch of salt and 200ml water, mix, then strain through a sieve.
2. Pour into a bowl, skim off the foam, steam over low heat for 15 minutes, then turn off the heat and let it rest, covered, for about 5 minutes.
3. Make a sauce with 1 part oyster sauce, 1 part oligosaccharide syrup, and 1/2 part each of soy sauce and sesame oil, then pour it over the steamed egg.

_en.title: Conchiglie Pasta Salad
_en.intro:
20230527 #breakfastdiary 772, 20°C/cloudy
Rain hurrying summer along, and a seafood metaphor to match — #ConchiglieSalad.
1. Boil the conchiglie pasta in salted water.
2. Sear shiitake mushrooms in a hot pan with olive oil, then use the remaining heat to cook the zucchini.
3. Blanch the peas with minimal water, then add a bit more water and blanch the mussels.
4. Combine 1 through 3 in a bowl and dress with a vinaigrette. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

_en.title: Poached Egg and Pea Salad
_en.intro:
20230526 #breakfastdiary 771, 19°C/mostly cloudy, 21min/workout(U)
Even frozen peas, blanched with just a little water, bring out a lovely, subtle sweetness.
1. Once the water boils, turn off the heat, add 1 part vinegar, wait a moment, then gently slip in the egg to poach it quietly.
2. Blanch the peas with minimal water, plate them together with the poached egg, and top with a vinaigrette. Finish with parmesan. #PeaAndPoachedEggSalad
This is a recipe from #MyLocalFoodSalad.

_en.title: Korean Melon Salad
_en.intro:
20230525 #breakfastdiary 770, 15°C/partly cloudy
'Its flowers bloom fine, and its fruit is bountiful' —
a line from Canto 2 of the Yongbieocheonga (Songs of the Dragons Flying to Heaven); this really is the season when flowers are lovely and fruit grows abundant.
1. Wash one Korean melon well and peel it with a julienne peeler (the kind used for som tam).
2. Cut it in half, scoop out the seeds, strain the juice, and mix in white balsamic, salt, and pepper to make a dressing.
3. Slice the halved melon neatly, arrange on a plate, and spoon over the dressing from step 2.

올 여름의 할 일은 모르는 사람의 그늘을 읽는 일
(김경인, 올 여름의 할 일)

Right in the middle of COVID, around this time in '21, outside Kyobo Bookstore — the #GwanghwamunGeulpan (Gwanghwamun banner poem), a thing that doesn't change no matter how much time passes.
Today's breakfast is a very summery lemon parsley burrata toast.

카펠리니(면)는 차갑게 먹는 콜드파스타에 잘 어울린다. 명사처럼 쓰이는 동사, 마리네이드(한) 토마토 파스타
(토마토 마리네이드)
1. 방울토마토에 칼집을 내고 뜨거운 물에 데친 후 찬물에 담가 껍질을 벗긴다. 
2. 양파 반 개 다지고, 올리브오일 30ml, 발사믹(이 없구나, 꿀을 더 넣자,), 꿀, 레몬주스 각 10ml, 소금 조금 넣고 방울토마토를 버무린다. (바질 같은 허브가 있으면 넣자.) 냉장고에 넣어서 시원하게~
(파스타) 
1. 끓는 물에 카펠리니, 소금 약간 넣어 삶는다. 
2. 찬물에 면을 헹구고 볼에 담은 뒤 올리브오일을 넣는다. 
3. 접시에 면을 담고 토마토 마리네이드를 담는다. 파마산치즈를 올려도 좋다.

_en.title: Marinated Tomato Pasta
_en.intro:
20230521 #breakfastdiary 766, 19°C/partly cloudy, 26min/workout(U)
Capellini works beautifully in a cold pasta. A verb turned noun — marinated tomato pasta.
(Marinated tomatoes)
1. Score the cherry tomatoes, blanch in hot water, then transfer to cold water and peel.
2. Mince half an onion, then toss with the cherry tomatoes, 30ml olive oil, balsamic (oh wait, none left — add more honey instead), honey, 10ml lemon juice each, and a little salt. (Add basil or another herb if you have it.) Chill in the fridge to serve cold.
(Pasta)
1. Boil the capellini in salted water.
2. Rinse the noodles in cold water, transfer to a bowl, and toss with olive oil.
3. Plate the noodles and top with the marinated tomatoes. Parmesan on top is a nice touch too.

A flour-free, low-carb pizza absolutely loaded with vegetables.

_en.title: Shakshuka (Eggs in Hell)
_en.intro:
20230519 #breakfastdiary 764, 17°C/clear, 21min/workout(Y)
The mobile convenience that's crept into PC —
Reading the first line describing Naver's homepage redesign, the last few decades flashed before my eyes; I really am a dinosaur.
Served with pita bread, an overcooked (thanks to poor heat control) eggs-in-hell 🥲
I clearly cooked the eggs too long, but there's no undoing it now.
1. Heat olive oil in a pot and sauté minced garlic and onion.
2. Pour in the tomato sauce. (If it looks too thick, add about 1/4 cup of water.)
3. Add the eggs and mozzarella, cover, and wait until the cheese melts.
4. Sprinkle in some sliced scallions (parsley would be nice, but this works too).

_en.title: Greek-Style Cabbage Salad
_en.intro:
20230518 #breakfastdiary 763, 18°C/cloudy, 21min/workout(C)
At some point, Gwangju stopped being, for me, a proper noun naming a single city, and became a common noun for a span of time where human violence and human dignity coexisted in their most extreme forms. I no longer knew what I could possibly say about the cruelty that runs through the massacres of the New World, Auschwitz, Bosnia, and the Kanto and Nanjing massacres — and, in spite of it all, the fragile gestures of people who desperately tried to do something in the face of that violence.
(Novelist Han Kang, on memories of May 18th and 'The Brothers Lionheart')
A Greek-style cabbage salad, minus the feta.
1. Mince the cabbage, onion, scallion, and parsley, and put them in a bowl.
2. Add 3 parts olive oil, 3 parts lemon juice, salt, and pepper, and mix.
3. Plate it and finish with a generous sprinkle of sesame seeds.

_en.title: Scallion Cream Cheese Salmon Bagel
_en.intro:
20230516 #breakfastdiary 761, 18°C/clear, 20min/workout(Y)
Young green onions are called silpa. Loaded up on silpa to make a cream cheese spread. #ScallionCreamCheeseSalmonBagel
1. Mix 100g cream cheese (about half a tub), 3 parts scallions (or to taste), 2 parts honey, a good pinch of salt, and pepper, until well combined.
2. Halve the bagel, toast in a pan, then spread generously with the cream cheese from step 1.
3. Top with shallot (no onion on hand) and smoked salmon.

_en.title: Pea and Green Bean Salad
_en.intro:
20230514 #breakfastdiary 759, 19°C/partly cloudy, 21min/workout(U)
Something I learned today: string beans, young kidney beans, and green beans are all the same thing. Though shouldn't 'string bean' really be called 'bean string' instead?
1. Boil the peas and green beans with minimal water.
2. Heat olive oil in a pan and sauté sliced garlic. Add the peas and green beans and cook them together briefly.
3. Plate the cooked vegetables and top with sliced soft-boiled egg.
4. Finish with vinaigrette, pepper, and parmesan.
This is a recipe from #MyFrenchStyleSalad.

intro:

많은 브랜드가 사람들의 마음에 가닿고자 시각 매체에만 의존하죠. 이젠 다른 방법들 역시 찾아만 합니다.
(라자 라자만나르, 마스터카드 CMO) 
그래서 마스터카드는 시각을 자극하는 일반적인 광고 외에도 향수(후각)를 만들고, 마카롱(미각), 음악(청각)을 제공한다. 그리고 그 가운데 제일 인상적인 건 시각장애인들을 위한, 카드 한 면에 새긴 노치(촉각)다. 
반드시 마케팅 예산이 많다고 이런 걸 할 수 있는 건 아니지만, 분명한 건 예산이 없으면 못한다. 
*노치: 카드 표면이나 모서리에 작게 낸 흠집
어제 조식의 실패를 거울 삼아, 
1. 끓는 물에 소금소금 펜네를 삶고 건져낸 뒤 올리브오일을 두른다. 
2. 애호박은 두툼하게 잘라서 달군 팬에 올리브오일 두르고 앞뒤로 한 번씩만 굽는다. 
3. 끓는 물에 완두콩을 데친다. 
4. 볼에 펜네, 애호박, 완두콩, 페스토를 넣고 뒤섞뒤섞 #애호박바질페스토펜네
#나의로컬푸드샐러드 레시피 입니다.

_en.title: Zucchini Basil Pesto Penne
_en.intro:
20230513 #breakfastdiary 758, 17°C/mostly clear
Many brands rely only on visual media to reach people's hearts. Now, though, they're looking for other ways too.
(Raja Rajamannar, Mastercard CMO)
That's why, beyond the usual eye-catching ads, Mastercard also makes a fragrance (smell), macarons (taste), and music (hearing). And the most striking piece of all is a small notch cut into one edge of the card (touch), designed for people who are visually impaired.
Having a big marketing budget doesn't guarantee you can do something like this, but one thing's certain — without any budget, you definitely can't.
*Notch: a small mark or groove cut into the surface or edge of a card
Learning from yesterday's breakfast failure —
1. Boil the penne in salted water, drain, and toss with olive oil.
2. Cut the zucchini into thick slices and sear in a hot pan with olive oil, just once on each side.
3. Blanch the peas in boiling water.
4. Toss the penne, zucchini, peas, and pesto together in a bowl. #ZucchiniBasilPestoPenne
This is a recipe from #MyLocalFoodSalad.
While we're at it, let's go all in on zucchini — #ZucchiniBasilPestoPenne
1. Boil the penne in salted water, drain, and toss with olive oil.
2. Cut the zucchini into thick slices and sear in a hot pan with olive oil, just once on each side.
3. Blanch the peas in boiling water.
4. Toss the penne, zucchini, peas, and pesto together in a bowl.
This is a recipe from #MyLocalFoodSalad.

title: 사과브리치즈토스트 토스트
intro:
20230504, #조식다이어리 749, 17도/흐림
1학년 공부 중에 제일 중요한 공부는 뭘까요? 공동체 생활의 기본을 배우는 것입니다. 특히 1학년은 사회화가 필요한 시기라 다른 학년보다 적응 활동이 많이 필요합니다.
(중략) 
아이들의 사회화 과정은 아름답지 않습니다.힘들고 어렵고 괴로운 일들이 더 많지요. 부모나 교사보다 아이 자신이 제일 힘듭니다. 친구들의 반응이 항상 내 맘처럼 나를 위해 돌아가지 않기 때문이지요. :) 내 의도는 이게 아닌데 왜 친구는 이 렇게 반응할까 속상합니다. 다툼이 생기면 억울합니다. 선생님도 내 마음을 몰라주는 것 같습니다. 아이는 이런 하루 하루를 보내며 조금씩 성장해 나갑니다.
(출처: 초등샘Z 트위터) 
사회화 과정은 초등학교 1학년 때만 경험하는 게 아니다. 
식재료도 떨어지고 뭔가 한 없이 귀찮은 아침엔 #사과브리치즈토스트 
1. 달군 팬에 빵을 올리고 앞뒤로 올리브오일, 바삭하게 굽는다. 
2. 빵 위에 브리 치즈를 올리고 토치로 굽는다. 사과를 올리고 (호두를 사과 위에 고정시켜 줄) 꿀과 호두

_en.title: Apple Brie Toast
_en.intro:
20230504 #breakfastdiary 749, 17°C/cloudy
What's the most important thing to learn in first grade? Learning the basics of community life. First grade especially is a time when kids need socialization, so it takes more adjusting than other grades.
(omitted)
The socialization process for kids isn't pretty. There's more struggle, difficulty, and hardship than anything else. The child themselves has it hardest, harder than either parents or teachers, because friends don't always respond the way you'd hope. :) You wonder why a friend reacts that way when that's not what you meant at all — it stings. When conflicts happen, it feels unfair. Even the teacher seems not to understand how you feel. Kids grow up little by little, living through days like these.
(Source: Elementary Teacher Z, Twitter)
Socialization isn't something you only go through in first grade.

title: 나의문화유산답사기 계란덮밥 양파계란덮밥
intro:
20230502, #조식다이어리 747, 13도/한때흐림, 21분/운동(U) 
“그림에는 그것을 아는 자, 사랑하는 자, 보는 자, 모으는 자가 있다. 한갓 쌓아두는 것이라 면 잘 본다고 할 수 없고, 본다고 해도 칠해진 것밖에 분별하지 못하면 아직 사랑한다고는 할 수 없다. 사랑한다고 해도 오직 채색과 형태 만을 추구한다면 아직 안다고 할 수 없다. 안다 는 것은 화법은 물론이고 눈에 잘 드러나지 않 는 오묘한 이치와 정신까지 알아보는 것을 말 한다. 그러므로 그림의 묘미는 잘 안다는 데 있 으며 알게 되면 참으로 사랑하게 되고, 사랑하 게 되면 참되게 보게 되고, 볼줄 알게 되면 모 으게 되나니 그때 수장한 것은 한갓 쌓아두는 것과는 다른 것이다.”
유홍준 교수가 #나의문화유산답사기 서문에 쓴, "알면 보이고 보이면 사랑하게 되나니 그때 보이는 것은 이미 예전과 같지 않으리라."의 출처, 정조 때 문장가 유한준 글
그런 게 어디 그림 뿐일까? 
1. 따뜻한 물 한 컵에 다시마 한 조각 넣어 감칠맛 가득 육수를 준비한다. (생략 가능) 
2. 팬에 기름 두르고 양파 한 개 썰어서 넣는다. 
3. 양파가 투명해지면 준비한 육수를 붓고 간장1, 미림1, 설탕1 넣는다. 
4. 불을 끄고, 계란 두 개 적당히 풀어 넣는다. (아, 계란이 한 개 뿐이구나,) 적당히 익으면 밥 위에 붓는다.

_en.title: Onion and Egg Rice Bowl
_en.intro:
20230502 #breakfastdiary 747, 13°C/partly cloudy, 21min/exercise(U)
"In painting, there are those who know it, those who love it, those who merely look at it, and those who collect it. If all you do is hoard paintings, you can't be said to really look at them; and if you look but only make out the paint on the surface, you can't yet be said to love them. Even if you love them, if all you're after is color and form, you can't yet be said to know them. To know a painting means to grasp not only its technique but the subtle principle and spirit that don't readily meet the eye. So the true pleasure of painting lies in truly knowing it — once you know it, you come to truly love it; once you love it, you come to truly see it; once you can truly see, you come to collect; and what you collect then is something altogether different from mere hoarding."
This appears in the preface Professor Yu Hong-june wrote for #mytreasuredheritage — the source of the line "Once you know, you see; once you see, you come to love; and what you see then is no longer what it once was" is a piece by Yu Han-jun, a writer of King Jeongjo's era.
Is that really true only of paintings?
1. Steep a piece of dried kelp in a cup of warm water to make a savory broth. (Optional)
2. Heat oil in a pan and add one sliced onion.
3. Once the onion turns translucent, pour in the broth and add 1 soy sauce, 1 mirin, 1 sugar.
4. Turn off the heat and pour in two lightly beaten eggs. (Oh — turns out I only had one egg.) Once it's cooked to your liking, pour it over rice.

_en.title: Tenshinhan (Crab and Egg Rice Bowl)
_en.intro:
20230428 #breakfastdiary 742, 9°C/sunny, 21min/exercise(Y)
Just like jjajangmyeon, Japan has its own localized dishes too — one of them is tenshinhan, a crab-stick and egg rice bowl.
1. Simmer 200cc water, 2 sugar, 2 mirin, 1 soy sauce, 1 oyster sauce, adding starch to thicken as needed, to make the sauce ahead of time. (If you're sensitive to sweetness, use 1 sugar.)

3. Cover the rice with the egg and pour the prepared sauce over it.

title: 시어링 리버스시어링 안심스테이크
intro:
20230422, #조식다이어리 736, 15도/흐림, 21분/운동(Y) 
센불에 기름 듬뿍, 튀길 듯이 스테이크를 구우면 겉은 바삭, 마이야르 반응이 일어나는데 이 과정을 #시어링 #Searing 이라고 한다. 하지만 말이 쉽지, 겉은 타고 속은 익지 않는 경우가 대부분이(라고 한)다. 고기를 즐기는 편은 아니라서 고기를 구울 일이 거의 없으니, 이 비싸고 낯선 식재료를 어찌 다뤄야 하나 고민하다가 알게 된 것이 #리버스시어링 이다. 
(수비드처럼 하지만 수비드 기계 대신) 오븐을 이용, 저온에서 장시간, 고기를 균일하게 익힌 뒤 간단하게 시어링하는 조리법으로, 비교적 실패 확률이 낮다고 한다. 
-안심을 상온에 뒀다가, 90도 오븐에 40분 익힌다. (소금, 후추로 마리네이드 된 안심이다.) 
-팬에 식용유를 붓고 30초씩 두 번 뒤집고, 버터, 로즈마리를 넣고 다시 30초씩 두 번 뒤집으며 베이스팅한다. 
이런 계획이었지만 막상 눈앞에서 고기가 익어가며 사방으로 기름이 튀는 순간을 맞이하면 호흡은 가빠지고 손놀림은 거칠어지며 30초, 두 번 등의 정량적 계획은 무쓸모가
됐다. 찍어 놓은 영상을 보니 시어링을 꽤 많이 충분히 했고 덕분에 계획했던 미디움웰던은 저 세상으로 가고, 웰던만 남았다. 
역시 어떤 일을 맞닥뜨린 순간, 성공과 실패를 좌우하는 건 치밀한 계획보다 역시 숙련된 손놀림이다. 결국 많이 해보는 수 밖에 없다. 
스테이크의 경우, 고기를 그리 좋아하지는 않으니 앞으로 능수능란하게 조리해서 먹을 일은 없지 않을까 싶다.

_en.title: Reverse-Seared Tenderloin Steak
_en.intro:
20230422 #breakfastdiary 736, 15°C/cloudy, 21min/exercise(Y)
When you sear a steak in plenty of oil over high heat, almost frying it, the outside turns crisp and the Maillard reaction kicks in — that process is called #searing. Easier said than done, though: most of the time the outside burns before the inside is cooked. I don't really go for meat, so I rarely cook it, and while I was wondering how to handle this expensive, unfamiliar ingredient, I came across #reversesearing.
It's a method that uses the oven instead of a sous vide machine (though the idea is similar) — cooking the meat evenly at a low temperature over a long time, then finishing with a quick sear. Supposedly it has a fairly low failure rate.
-Let the tenderloin come to room temperature, then cook it in a 90°C oven for 40 minutes. (The tenderloin was marinated beforehand with salt and pepper.)
-Pour oil in a pan and flip it twice, 30 seconds each side; then add butter and rosemary and baste while flipping twice more, 30 seconds each side.
That was the plan, but the moment the meat actually started cooking in front of me, oil spattering everywhere, my breathing sped up, my hands got clumsy, and all those neat numbers — 30 seconds, twice — went out the window. Watching the video I took afterward, I'd clearly seared it quite a bit more than planned, so my intended medium-well went out the window too, leaving just well-done.
Once again: in the moment you're actually facing a task, what decides success or failure isn't a meticulous plan so much as practiced hands. In the end, there's no substitute for doing it many times.
As for steak, since I'm not that big on meat, I doubt I'll ever get around to cooking it skillfully.

한국사회에서 ‘되다’의 잦은 사용 역시 어쩌면 어떤 상황에서든 책임을 회피하려는 안전장치를 마련하기 위해 시작‘된’ 것일지도 모른다. ‘생각하다’와 ‘생각되다’를 나란히 놓고 보면 의미의 차이는 분명하다. ‘생각되다’에서는 생각의 행위자도 명확하지 않고 그 주체 역시 애매모호하다.
(로버트 파우저, ‘하다’ 대신 ‘되다’…생각의 행위자를 감추는 시대) 
#내부자들 의 논설위원, 이강희의 대사 중에 이런 게 있다. “끝에 단어 세 개만 좀 바꿉시다. ‘볼 수 있다’가 아니라 ‘매우 보여진다’로.”

_en.title: Inside Men Strawberry Mango Salad
_en.intro:
20230414, #BreakfastDiary 7289, 11°C/cloudy
In Korean society, the frequent use of the passive voice might itself have started as a safety mechanism for avoiding responsibility in any situation. Set '생각하다' (to think) next to '생각되다' (to be thought) and the difference in meaning is clear - in the passive form, the one doing the thinking is never named, and the subject stays vague.
(Robert Fouser, "'To Be Done' Instead of 'To Do' - An Age That Hides the Agent of Thought")
There's a line from Lee Kang-hee, the editorial writer in Inside Men: "Let's just change three words at the end. Not 'you can see it,' but 'it is very much seen.'"
Strawberries, rosemary, olive oil and balsamic, half a mango.

_en.title: Apple Mango Juice
_en.intro:
20230413 #breakfastdiary 728, 6°C/mostly sunny, released from COVID quarantine
(During what people call the global pandemic years) over the past few years, whenever a coworker, friend, family member, or neighbor came down with COVID-19, I'd offer heartfelt-sounding words — how hard that must be, hang in there, you'll feel better soon. But now that I've actually gone through it myself, I realize all those well-wishes I gave were, in a sense, empty — meaning, pain you haven't lived through, you can't really understand. Maybe this is what Shin Hyung-cheol meant when he said you can only truly know someone else's pain and sorrow by studying and experiencing it yourself.
With my sense of smell still not back and barely able to taste anything, this felt like a bit of fresh-stimulation therapy.
1 apple, a good amount of frozen mango, 2 napa cabbage leaves, 180ml water, 2T lime juice #applemangojuice

_en.title: Shiitake Mushroom Pasta
_en.intro:
20230404 #breakfastdiary 726, 12°C/cloudy, 21min/workout(U)
I was reading an interview with the late Ryuichi Sakamoto and got curious about the idea of #wabisabi he talked about, so I've been looking into it and mulling it over.
A rematch with yesterday's breakfast, mushroom pasta.
- Melt butter in a pan, toss in minced mushrooms and pepper, and sauté, sauté, sauté.
- Add a splash of pasta water and some larger-cut mushrooms, sauté, sauté, sauté.
- Add the boiled noodles, a bit more pasta water, and grate, grate, grate in some parmesan.
- Turn off the heat, stir in an egg yolk, and toss, toss, toss.

_en.title: Spam Ketchup Fusilli
_en.intro:
20230402 #breakfastdiary 724, 17°C/sunny, 36min/workout(U)
I happened to be out of spaghetti, so I made this #spamketchuppasta with fusilli instead.
- Bring 1 liter of water with 2T soy sauce to a boil. Once it's boiling, add the fusilli and cook until al dente.
- Mash the Spam, add oil, and stir-fry, stir-fry in the pan.
- Add onion, minced garlic, 1T sugar, and 1T soy sauce in order, stir-fry, stir-fry, stir-fry, then add 2T ketchup.
- Add the boiled fusilli and the soy-sauce pasta water, and stir-fry, stir-fry, stir-fry, stir-fry.

_en.intro:

_en.title: Green Papaya Som Tam
_en.intro:
20230326 #breakfastdiary 717, 9°C/sunny, 35min/workout(Y)
Last summer in Bangkok I picked up a dedicated som tam grater (for about 1,500 won), and it slices green papaya into just the right shreds every time. So today's breakfast version skips the chili — a mild #greenpapayasomtam.
Pound a little garlic, 1T sugar, 1T fish sauce, and 2T lime juice together with tomato, lightly.
Add the shredded green papaya and carrot, pounding until the dressing soaks in well. Toss in the peanuts and mix, mix.

intro:

블룸버그에서 만든 #프렛지수 는 #프레타망제 매장의 매출을 토대로 도시의 활동(회복)성을 확인하는 지표로 쓰인다. 런던, 뉴욕, 파리, 홍콩 등의 대도시에 매장이 있어서 팬대믹 전후를 도시의 활동성을 비교하는데 유용하다고, 
코로나 이전 1을 기준으로 히드로공항의 프랫지수는 1.4정도 된다고 한다. @longblack.co 
빠른 속도로 예전으로 돌아가고 있다는 증거다. 
보리밥에 김자반, 참기름을 두르고 버터헤드 레터스를 다져서 넣는다. 
멍게는 내장을 떼내고 소금을 조금 뿌려 조물조물, 흐르는 물에 헹군다. 
멍게에 다진 마늘, 손바닥으로 (으드득) 다진 참깨, 참기름, 고추 썰어넣고 SSG SSG, 봄을 부르는 #멍게비빔밥

_en.title: Sea Squirt Bibimbap
_en.intro:
20230323 #breakfastdiary 714, 13°C/cloudy, 21min/workout(Y)
The #pretindex, created by Bloomberg, tracks sales at #pretamanger stores as a way to gauge how active (or recovered) a city is. Since Pret has locations in big cities like London, New York, Paris, and Hong Kong, it's a handy way to compare urban activity before and after the pandemic.
With pre-COVID activity set at 1, Heathrow Airport's Pret Index is now sitting at around 1.4. @longblack.co
Proof that things are snapping back to normal fast.
Drizzle sesame oil over barley rice with crumbled seasoned laver, then mix in chopped butterhead lettuce.
Remove the innards from the sea squirt, sprinkle with a little salt, massage gently, and rinse under running water.
Add minced garlic, sesame seeds crushed by hand (with a satisfying crunch), sesame oil, and sliced chili pepper to the sea squirt, mix mix — a #seasquirtbibimbap to welcome spring.

_en.intro:
20230322 #breakfastdiary 713, 8°C/mostly sunny, 21min/workout(C)
The trendy #bananabread everyone's making lately.

_en.intro:

- Melt a generous knob of butter in a pan and sauté sliced onions.

title: 딸기샐러드 딸기
intro:
20230316, #조식다이어리 707, 0도/흐림, 21분/운동
나는 60살이고 이제야 첫 오스카상을 수상했다. 나는 인내심에 대해 잘 알고 있으며, 사회가 여성에게 기대하는 바를 너무 잘 알고 있다. 또한 내 경험은 위기의 최전선에서 싸우는 여성 영웅들과 결코 비교할 수 없다는 것도 잘 알고 있다. 하지만 내가 커리어에서 기쁨을 누리는 지금 이 순간에 할 수 있는 일이 하나 있다. 그건 바로 인정받지 못할 때가 많은 사람들, 즉 지역 사회를 재건하고 어린이와 노인을 돌보며 식탁에 음식을 올리는 여성들에게 스포트라이트를 돌리는 것이다. 이들에게 가장 큰 영향을 미치는 의사 결정이 내려질 때 더 이상 그 자리에서 소외되지 않도록 해야 한다.
(양자경, 세상 모든 여성에게 스포트라이트를 돌립니다, 뉴욕타임즈, @alookso) 
딸기, 세상에서 제일 예쁜 부라타치즈, 바질에 올리브오일, 발사믹, 후추후추후추후추 #딸기샐러드

_en.title: Strawberry Burrata Salad
_en.intro:
20230316 #breakfastdiary 707, 0°C/cloudy, 21min/workout
I'm sixty years old, and I've only just won my first Oscar. I know a great deal about patience, and I know all too well what society expects of women. I also know my own experience can't compare to that of the women fighting on the front lines of crisis. But there's one thing I can do, in this moment of joy in my career — turn the spotlight onto those who so often go unrecognized: the women rebuilding communities, caring for children and the elderly, and putting food on the table. They shouldn't be left out of the room when the decisions that affect them most are being made.
(Michelle Yeoh, “I'm Turning the Spotlight on Every Woman in the World,” The New York Times, @alookso)
Strawberries, the most beautiful burrata cheese in the world, and basil with olive oil, balsamic, and lots and lots of pepper #strawberrysalad

_en.title: Beef Broth Fusilli
_en.intro:
20230306, #breakfastdiary 697, 0°C/mostly cloudy, 0min exercise
Boil 500ml of water and drop in a #cookingqueen #eggbrothcube — the rich, deep flavor of Korean beef packed into one little ball, the secret to an easy, no-fuss beef stock.
Heat olive oil and butter in a pan and sauté the chopped onion. Once it turns translucent, add the parboiled fusilli and warm it through.
Pour in half the stock and simmer; once it reduces, add the rest and let it simmer gently until it thickens.
Once the fusilli has soaked up plenty of flavor, plate it and top with chopped parsley and parmesan cheese.

Long ago in America, French toast used to be called German toast.
Beat two eggs with milk and a pinch of salt, salt, then soak the bread in it.
Melt a good lump of butter in a pan and toast the egg-soaked (?) bread evenly on every side.
Move it to a plate and top with strawberries, apple mint, and powdered sugar. #frenchtoast
From this morning's paper, a line from Seo Kyung-seok's column: the 'death toll' from wars or accidents we hear about is certainly one measure, but it also has a way of numbing the imagination.

신형철 선생의 책을 가까이에 두고 생각날 때마다 집어든다. 
사랑받는 사람이 되는 가장 정확한 방법은 사랑받을 만한 사람이 되는 것이다. 정확한 길이기는 하지만, 쉽고 빠른 길은 아니다. 사랑받을 만한 사람이 되기 위해서는 타인과의 섬세하고 복잡한 커뮤니케이션에 성공해야 한다. 그 어렵고 느린 길을 걸을 능력도 의지도 없는 이들은 그 대신 권력을 가지려 한다. 권력을 얻어 명령의 주체가 되면 커뮤니케이션을 생략해도 된다고 믿기 때문이다.

_en.title: Red Cabbage and Tangerine Salad
_en.intro:
20230225, #breakfastdiary 689, 1°C/sunny, 27min exercise
I keep Shin Hyung-cheol's book close by and pick it up whenever something comes to mind.
The surest way to become someone who is loved is to become someone worth loving. It's the right path, but not an easy or a quick one. To become worth loving, you have to succeed at delicate, complicated communication with other people. Those who lack the ability or the will to walk that hard, slow road choose power instead — because once you hold power and become the one giving orders, you believe you can skip communication altogether.
(Shin Hyung-cheol, Sorrow Studying Sorrow)

_en.title: Red Cabbage Avocado Salad
_en.intro:
20230214, #breakfastdiary 678, -3°C/cloudy, 11min exercise
Red cabbage avocado salad.
Slice red cabbage lengthwise. Arrange on an oven pan and brush with a dressing of olive oil, salt, pepper, garlic powder, and cumin. Roast at 210°C for 30 minutes.
Transfer to a plate, mash half an avocado over it, then sprinkle with lime juice, salt, pepper, and chili powder.

_en.intro:

This is my #mylocalfoodsalad recipe.

달군 팬에 올리브오일, 시판 크레페를 펼치고 계란을 올린다. 소금, 후추 약간,

_en.title: Sikhye and Crepe
_en.intro:
20230129 #breakfastdiary 663, -5°C/partly cloudy, 11min/workout
A random little story about 'grain tea' —
#GokCha (literally 'grain tea') is a monk's euphemism for alcohol. The story goes that a Joseon-era monk, Great Master Jinmuk, felt a bit sheepish about drinking and started calling it 'tea' (cha) instead — and that's supposedly where the term comes from.
Songhwa Baegiljju, passed down for nearly 400 years by the head monk of Suwangsa Temple in Jeollabuk-do, is probably the best-known example of this kind of 'grain tea.' Alcohol was forbidden in temples, but it also served as a means of practice. I like to think that's not so different from enjoying a quiet drink alone now and then, just to listen to your inner voice.
A crepe eaten alongside #sikhye (sweet rice drink), which has a bit of that 'grain tea' feeling —
Heat a pan with olive oil, spread out a store-bought crepe, and crack an egg onto it. A little salt and pepper.
Fold the crepe neatly, then top with tomato, strawberry, banana, and avocado.
I debated finishing it with parmesan cheese or powdered sugar, then just ate it as is.

_en.intro:
20230128 #breakfastdiary 662, -8°C/partly cloudy, 27min/workout
A day when snow turns to rain
Another haze over the ashen sky, and
The great locomotive shrieks,
And my small heart trembles.
This parting comes too fast, so sadly,
From the one I love,
Who said we'd meet again at work —
Before the warmth of that hand, before the tear-drops dry,
The train turned its tail toward the mountain pass.
(Yun Dong-ju, Farewell)

There's been some buzz lately about a Korea Consumer Agency report on the durability of nonstick pan coatings. Apparently it involved scrubbing coated pans with a steel wool pad as a kind of stress test — I'm not entirely sure that's a fair method. As with most things in this world, it's probably best not to take it as gospel, just file it away as a data point.
Heat olive oil in a pan and sauté shiitake mushrooms with a little salt.

title: 서가에서 브로콜리아보카도샐러드 브로콜리
intro:
20230124, #조식다이어리 658, -18도/맑음, 36분/운동
오늘 아침, 잠이 덜 깨 눈을 반쯤 뜬 상태에서 읽었던, 글이 인상적이었다. 
그래도 우리 삶이 영화보다 나은 이유는 잡을 수 있는 온기 가 있기 때문이다.
내멋대로 '우와, 방금 영화 같았다.' 라고 생각하는 순간이 있다. 시험 시간, 1분 1초 촉박하게 흘러가는 속에 바쁘게 움직이는 손이 이상하게도 만족럽게 느껴질 때. 늦은 하교 시간 복도로 햇살이 늘어질 때, 그 사이로 발소리 하나만 울리고있을 때. 어느 날은 비가 쏟아지는데도 이상하게 마음이 뽀송했고 누군가 예고 없이 머리카락을 만지면 뒷목이 간지러웠다. 아, 진짜 조금만 더. 조금만 더 길었으면 좋겠다. 혹은, 내가 원하는 순간에 이곳으로 돌아올 수 있었으면 좋겠다. 난 초록이 우거진 틈새로 반짝이는 어느날의 거실을 자꾸만 들여다봤다. 해가 노을을 향해 꿀떡 넘어갈 때까지.
그러니까 이런 순간만이 영화 같다면 얼마나 좋아.
원하지 않아도 영화 같은 순간은 길고 긴 모의고사 시간에 시험지에 코를 박고 몰래 울었을 때. 그러면 안 되는 순간에 화를 내고 말았을 때. 누군가 나를 관객의 시선으로 참을성 있게 지켜보지 않았다면 이해받을 수 없는 감정에 휩쓸렸을 때다. 이상하네. 드라마 보면 이렇게 울고불고 해도 괜찮던데. 그들은 뭔가를 마구 쏟아내고, 있는 힘껏 불행해진 다음 컷, 하면 그만이지만 난 그게 아니라는 걸 실제로 그렇게 해 보고서야 알았다. 아무리 슬퍼도 나에겐 이 다음을 이어나 갈 의무가 있었다. 그렇게 하고 싶지 않아도 어쩔 수 없다. 우리에겐 컷, 해줄 사람이 없기 때문이다.
모든 것이 덧없던 빌런과는 정확히 반대로, 내겐 아무것도 덧없지 않아서 괴로웠다. 모든 것이 너무 소중했으므로 종국엔 똑같이 모든 걸 베이글 위에 올려버리고 싶었다. A컷 B컷으로 나누고 한정된 시간 안에 가장 효율적인 감동을 창출하기 위해 나의 어떤 장면도 생략할 수 없었다. 그러니 우리에게 허락된 이 비효율이 얼마나 귀한지. 어차피 모든 것을 지켜보는 이는 나 하나뿐이므로 다른 관객의 눈치를 보지 않아도 돼. 원한다면 마음에 드는 장면을 한없이, 한없이 길게 늘이고 반복해도 돼. 마음에 안 들면 중간에 내 마음대로 장르를 변경하고, 영화처럼 울고 웃다가도 멋없게 뒷수습해도 돼. 바로 이것이 영화 밖을 벗어난 우리의 권리다. 영화 건너에서는 느낄 수 없는 사람의 온가는 이 순간 탄생한다. 잘라내고, 생략하고, 다듬지 않은 채로 어수선하고 바지런하게 수습하 고 있을 장면이 대부분일 모습.
#서가에서 1월호 
잡을 수 있는 온기가 가득한 샐러드, 
-끓는 물에 브로콜리를 데친다. 
-아보카도 반 개는 큐브 모양으로 썬다. 
-피스타치오 껍질을 까고 잘게 다진다. 
-올리브오일 3, 와인비니거 1, 홀그레인머스타드 1/2 섞어 드레싱, 후추후추 
피스타치오를 곁들인 #브로콜리아보카도샐러드

_en.title: Broccoli Avocado Salad
_en.intro:
20230124 #breakfastdiary 658, -18°C/clear, 36min/workout
This morning, half-asleep with my eyes barely open, I read something that really struck me.
Still, the reason our lives are better than a movie is that they have a warmth we can actually hold.
There are moments when I think to myself, 'wow, that just felt like a movie.' Like during an exam, when time is racing by second by second and my hands, moving in a hurry, feel strangely satisfying. Or in the late-afternoon hallway after school, when the sunlight stretches long across the floor and the only sound is a single set of footsteps. Some days it rains and yet my heart feels oddly dry and warm, or someone touches my hair without warning and the back of my neck tingles. Ah, just a little more — I wish it had lasted a little longer. Or that I could come back to that exact moment whenever I wanted. I kept looking into some living room from some particular day, glittering through gaps in green leaves, until the sun sank all the way into the sunset.
So how wonderful would it be if only these moments were like a movie.
But the moments that feel like a movie without my wanting them to are the long, endless mock exam when I buried my face in the test paper and cried in secret. The times I ended up getting angry at moments I shouldn't have. The times I was swept up in feelings no one could understand, because no one was patiently watching me the way an audience watches a character. It's strange — in dramas, it's fine to cry and wail like that. The characters just pour everything out, become as miserable as they possibly can, and then, cut — that's it. But it was only by actually living through it that I learned that's not how it works for me. No matter how sad I was, I still had a duty to keep going to whatever came next. I have no choice, even if I don't want to. Because there's no one to call 'cut' for us.
Unlike the villain, for whom everything felt meaningless, nothing felt meaningless to me — and that was exactly what made it so painful. Everything mattered too much, so in the end I wanted to pile it all onto the same bagel anyway. Dividing things into take A and take B, unable to cut out a single scene of my own life in order to create the most efficient possible emotional payoff within a limited time. So how precious is this inefficiency we're allowed. Since I'm the only one watching everything anyway, I don't have to worry about any other audience. If I want, I can stretch out and replay a scene I love for as long as I like, endlessly. If I don't like something, I can change the genre halfway through on a whim, cry and laugh like in a movie, and clean up the mess afterward without it looking graceful at all. That is exactly the freedom we have outside the movies. A human warmth you could never feel on the other side of the screen is born in this very moment. Most of it will be scenes that are cut, skipped, left unpolished — messy but diligently cleaned up, one way or another.
#Seogaeseo, January issue
A salad full of the kind of warmth you can actually hold,
- Blanch broccoli in boiling water.
- Cut half an avocado into cubes.
- Shell pistachios and chop them finely.
- Mix olive oil (3), wine vinegar (1), and wholegrain mustard (1/2) for the dressing, and finish with pepper, pepper.
#BroccoliAvocadoSalad with pistachios

- Shred king oyster mushrooms along the grain with a fork. (Shredded this way, king oyster mushroom looks just like chicken breast.)

- Brush bread with olive oil and toast both sides in a hot pan.

_en.title: Oven-Roasted Enoki Mushrooms
_en.intro:
20230121 #breakfastdiary 656, -7°C/clear
Humans only truly change through direct experience, which means the only thing that can really change me is the trial and error I've already lived through. (...) Even after learning something the hard way, we go right back to repeating the same mistakes — that's just what it is to be human. In that sense, life is made up of repetitions. So how difficult it must be to slowly, gradually become a better person.
(Shin Hyung-cheol, Studying Sorrow's Sorrow)
I've been keeping Shin Hyung-cheol's book close by, reading a little at a time.
Lay out the prettiest enoki mushrooms in the world in a neat row, drizzle with olive oil, salt, salt, pepper, pepper, and roast in a 180°C oven for 20 minutes. Add a few walnuts on the side. #ovenroastedenokimushrooms

title: 토마토샐러드 모닝루틴 토마토
intro:
20230119, #조식다이어리 654, -7도/대체로흐림, 11분/운동
오늘자 신문, 
1950년대 이후부터 외국어 평가기준은 말하기, 듣기, 읽기, 쓰기 전반을 평가해, ‘사용할 수 없다’(0단계)부터 ‘교육받은 원어민과 동일한 수준’(5단계)까지 단계별로 평가가 이뤄졌다. 대부분 외교관은 ‘전문적인 수준으로 구사할 수 있는’(3단계) 수준 도달을 목표로 삼았고, 일반적으로 ‘외국어에 유창한 이들’은 4단계, ‘원어민에 가까운 수준’이면 4+단계로 보았다.
그런데 2022년부터 새롭게 적용한 기준에는 흥미로운 변화가 보인다. ‘교육받은 원어민과 동일한 수준’인 5단계와 ‘원어민에 가까운 수준’인 4+단계를 ‘4단계’로 통합하면서 ‘원어민’이라는 말을 없애고, ‘고급 능력’이라고 이름 붙였다. 외국어 학습에서 ‘원어민 같은’ 실력을 갖춰야 한다는 목표를 삭제한 것이다. 이는 2000년대 이후 외국어교육에서 ‘원어민’을 바라보는 시선의 변화를 반영한 것이다.
(로버트 파우저, ‘원어민주의’ 시대 막을 내리면서) 
미국 외교관들에게 외국어를 가르치는 외교교육원 평가기준의 변화에서 시대의 변화가 엿보인다. 원어민처럼 말하는 능력보다는 “서로 다른 문화에 대한 상호 이해와 적응 능력이 중요“해진 것이다. 
큰 토마토, 작은 토마토에 세상에서 제일 탐스러운 부라타치즈, 올리브오일과 발사믹 #토마토샐러드

_en.title: Tomato Salad
_en.intro:
20230119 #breakfastdiary 654, -7°C/mostly cloudy, 11min/workout
Today's newspaper —
Since the 1950s, foreign language proficiency has been evaluated across speaking, listening, reading, and writing, on a scale running from 'unable to use the language' (level 0) to 'equivalent to an educated native speaker' (level 5). Most diplomats aimed for 'professional working proficiency' (level 3), while those generally considered 'fluent in a foreign language' were rated level 4, and those at a 'near-native level' were rated 4+.
But an interesting shift appears in the new standard adopted in 2022. Level 5 ('equivalent to an educated native speaker') and level 4+ ('near-native level') were merged into a single 'level 4,' dropping the term 'native speaker' altogether in favor of 'advanced proficiency.' In other words, the goal of achieving 'native-like' skill was removed from foreign language learning altogether. This reflects a shift, since the 2000s, in how foreign language education has come to view the whole idea of the 'native speaker.'
(Robert Fouser, 'As the Age of Native-Speakerism Comes to a Close')
This change in the evaluation standards of the Foreign Service Institute, which teaches foreign languages to American diplomats, hints at a broader shift of the times. What matters now isn't sounding like a native speaker so much as 'the ability to understand and adapt across different cultures.'
Big tomatoes and small tomatoes with the most tempting burrata cheese in the world, olive oil, and balsamic. #tomatosalad

_en.title: Asparagus Tomato Salad
_en.intro:
20230117 #breakfastdiary 652, -8°C/cloudy, 11min/workout
Sear the prettiest asparagus in the world in a hot pan with salt, salt, pepper, pepper.
Once it's about halfway cooked, add halved cherry tomatoes and sear those too. Wipe out the pan and toast a handful of walnuts — toasting them in the pan really brings out their nuttiness.
Transfer everything to a plate and shave over pecorino cheese, grate, grate, grate — an asparagus tomato salad finished with #pecorinocheese.

title: 연어빠삐요뜨 모닝루틴 빠삐요뜨
intro:
20230116, #조식다이어리 651, -8도/청명함, 11분/운동
기본적으로 기계식 시계에서 롤렉스가 차지하는 위상은 내구성이다. 실제로 롤렉스는 항공시계와 다이버 시계 부문에서 추종할 수 없는 위치를 차지하고 있고, 비가 오나 눈이 오나 허구헌날 야지를 헤매며 게릴라전을 수행해야 했던 체에게 시계의 내구성은 그 무엇보다도 중요했을 것이다. 시계가 언제나 정확한 시간을 가리키고 있어야 작전을 수행할 수 있고, 그렇기 때문에 그는 필요하다면 그 시절 자본주의의 총아와도 같았던 물건을 가지고 다녔던 것 뿐이다.
(김현성, 체 게바라는 롤렉스를 찼다: 위선자보다 위선무새가 더 나쁜 법입니다 @alookso )
혁명가와 명품 시계가 도무지 어울리지 않는다는 말이 있지만 체가 처한 상황을 떠올려 보면 쉽게 수긍이 갈 것이다. 그와는 다른 이유지만 (와치 페이스를) GMT로 바꿨다. 
달군 팬에 올리브오일을 두르고 애호박과 아스파라거스를 데친다. (그냥 넣어도 좋지만 몇몇 재료는 이렇게 구우면 본연의 맛이 더 올라온다.) 
연어는 물기를 닦아내고 후추후추, 소금소금 해둔다. 
팬에 종이호일을 깔고 애호박, 아스파라거스, 연어 그리고 토마토, 마늘, 감자, 레몬 등 각종 야채를 썰어 넣는다. 올리브오일, 소금, 후추 그리고 화이트와인을 살짝 붓는다. 
종이호일로 가장자리를 덮고 200도 오븐에 25분 굽는다. #연어빠삐요뜨

연어는 물기를 닦아내고 후추후추, 소금소금 해둔다. 
팬에 종이호일을 깔고 애호박, 아스파라거스, 연어 그리고 토마토, 마늘, 감자, 레몬 등 각종 야채를 썰어 넣는다. 올리브오일, 소금, 후추 그리고 화이트와인을 살짝 붓는다.

At its core, what defines a Rolex among mechanical watches is durability. Rolex genuinely holds an unrivaled place in aviation and diver's watches, and for someone like Che, who had to trek through rough terrain in all weather while running a guerrilla campaign, a watch's durability would have mattered more than almost anything else. Operations depended on a watch always showing the correct time, so if that meant carrying around an item that was practically a darling of the capitalist system of the day, so be it.
(Kim Hyun-sung, 'Che Guevara Wore a Rolex: A Hypocrite Parrot Is Worse Than a Hypocrite,' @alookso)

Fold the parchment paper over the edges and bake at 200°C for 25 minutes. #salmonpapillote

_en.title: Radish and Oyster Rice
_en.intro:
20230108 #breakfastdiary 645, 0°C/clear, 11min/workout
Rinse the rice and soak it for about 30 minutes. Add the soaked rice, along with the prettiest, sweetest radish in the world, and oysters, to a pot and cook for about 30 minutes.
Mix scallion, soy sauce, garlic, sugar, and sesame oil together, whisk it up, and spoon the sauce over the rice. In-season #radishoysterrice
#LivingTip: since radish and oysters already hold plenty of moisture, use less water than usual when cooking the rice. Adding the oysters right from the start lets their aroma fully infuse the rice — just don't expect the oysters to stay plump and springy though.

title: 모닝루틴 계란 베이컨
intro:
20230105, #조식다이어리 642, -9도/청명함, 11분/운동
2001년 티보의 회고전에 참여했던 마리아 프라터 큐레이터는 AP통신에 "유화 물감은 머랭처럼 보였고, 특히 케이크 그림에서는 진짜 케이크의 프로스팅과 같은 질감이 느껴졌다"며 "그림을 핥고 싶을 정도였다"고 말했다.
이런 그림으로 그는 1960년대 미국의 풍성함을 담아냈다. 로이 리히텐슈타인, 앤디 워홀 등과 함께 당대를 대표하는 팝 아티스트로 평가받기도 했다.
(연합뉴스, 달콤함 그려낸 팝 아티스트 웨인 티보 별세)
다만 웨인 티보 본인은 팝아트를 좋아하지도, 팝 아티스트로 평가받는 것에 동의하지도 않았다고. 
그는 2021년 12월 25일 향년 101세의 나이로 케이크, 아이스크림 등 수많은, 달콤한 작품을 남기고 자택에서 숨을 거뒀다. 
그의 Breakfast, 언젠가 한 번쯤 재현해보고 싶었던 풍경이다. 
써니사이드업 계란 두 개, 베이컨 세 장

_en.intro:
20230105, #breakfastdiary 642, -9°C/clear, 11min/exercise
Maria Porges, the curator who took part in Thiebaud's 2001 retrospective, told the AP that "the oil paint looked like meringue, and especially in the cake paintings, it had the same texture as real cake frosting" — "it made you want to lick the painting."
Through paintings like these, he captured the abundance of 1960s America. Alongside Roy Lichtenstein, Andy Warhol, and others, he was regarded as one of the leading Pop artists of his era.
(Yonhap News, Pop artist Wayne Thiebaud, who painted sweetness, passes away)
Thiebaud himself, though, never much liked Pop Art, nor did he agree with being labeled a Pop artist.
He passed away at his home on December 25, 2021, at the age of 101, leaving behind countless sweet works — cakes, ice cream, and more.
His painting Breakfast is a scene I'd always wanted to recreate someday.
Two sunny-side-up eggs, three strips of bacon

_en.title: New Year Smashed Broccoli
_en.intro:
20230103, #breakfastdiary 640, 0°C/clear, 0min/exercise
The digital economy is a competition for stealing attention. Today's sharpest statisticians, psychologists, and developers are all racing to find ways to erode users' willpower, and the result shows up as persuasive recommendation algorithms. To that end, Netflix tracks which scenes people rewatch, and mobile game apps analyze the background noise around their users.
Koo Bon-kwon, "New Year's Resolutions for the Digital Age"
Tastes shaped by algorithms inevitably grow uniform. As #newyear arrives, it's worth pausing to ask whether the tastes I hold (these days) are really my own.
1. Blanch the broccoli in boiling water.
2. Lay the broccoli in a hot pan and press it flat. Drizzle with olive oil and sear thoroughly on both sides along with sliced garlic.
3. Move it to a plate, then finish with lemon juice, red pepper flakes, and a generous grating of parmesan.
(For extra crispness, the oven might work better than the pan.)

title: 팬톤에서 토마토시금치랩 모닝루틴
intro:

2021년. 얼티밋 그레이Ultimate Gray와 일루미네이팅 옐로Illuminating Yellow가 선정됐어. 두 가지 색을 올해의 색으로 선정한 건 2016년 로즈 쿼츠rose quartz와 세레니티serenity 이후로 두 번째였지. 회색과 절묘하게 어우러지는 노란색. 팬데믹이 막 들이닥쳐 힘들어하던 사람들에게 팬톤이 던지는 위로였어.
(중략)
인간의 의지와 희망에 대한 보편적인 색을 골랐어요. 회색은 수백만 년 동안 존재해왔으며 결코 사라지지 않을 바위와 돌의 색이에요. 불굴의 의지를 나타내죠. 당신이 의지할 수 있는 건 항상 당신을 위해 거기 있을 거라는 의미입니다. 노란색은 어렸을 때부터 희망, 긍정, 기대할 만한 것을 의미해요. 인간의 정신에 필수적인 희망, 아름다운 햇살이 내리쬐는 하늘 등을 의미하죠.
팬톤 : 티파니 블루와 스타벅스 그린, 컬러 비즈니스를 개척하다, 롱블랙 @longblack.co
매년 12월, #팬톤에서 발표하는 다음 해 컬러로 한해를 맞이하는 루틴이 있다. 몇년 전 코로나의 한복판에서 그들이 빌표한 얼티밋 그레이Ultimate Gray와 일루미네이팅 옐로Illuminating Yellow는 상당히 인상적이었다. 
내년의 컬러는 비바 마젠타Viva Magenta, 삶을 축하하는 색이라고 한다. 
 
시판 또띠야는 팬에 굽는다. 토마토소스를 바르고 시금치, 방울 토마토를 올린다. 파마산치즈, 후추후추, 말아서 먹는 #토마토시금치랩

_en.title: Tomato Spinach Wrap
_en.intro:
20221229, #breakfastdiary 637, -7°C/clear, 11min/exercise
In 2021, Ultimate Gray and Illuminating Yellow were chosen. It was only the second time two colors were picked as Color of the Year, after Rose Quartz and Serenity in 2016. Gray, exquisitely paired with yellow. It was the comfort Pantone offered to a world just staggering under the pandemic's first blows.
(omitted)
We chose colors that speak to universal human resilience and hope. Gray is the color of rock and stone, which have existed for millions of years and will never disappear — it represents steadfastness, the sense that something you can lean on will always be there for you. Yellow has meant hope, optimism, and anticipation since childhood — the hope essential to the human spirit, a sky drenched in beautiful sunlight.
Pantone: How Tiffany Blue and Starbucks Green Pioneered the Color Business, Longblack @longblack.co
Every December, I have a small ritual of greeting the new year through the color #pantone announces for the year ahead. A few years back, in the thick of the pandemic, their pick of Ultimate Gray and Illuminating Yellow left quite an impression on me.
Next year's color, they say, is Viva Magenta — a color that celebrates life.

Pan-fry a store-bought tortilla. Spread on tomato sauce, then top with spinach and cherry tomatoes. Parmesan, a bit of pepper, and roll it up — #tomatospinachwrap

title: 조용한생활 이진숙 갈레뜨
intro:
20221225, #조식다이어리 634, -7도/맑음, 26분/운동
1822년에 나온 성 니콜라오스의 방문(클레멘트 무어)이라는 시집에 그의 외모가 묘사되어 있습니다. 장미빛 얼굴, 하얀 턱수염, 뚱뚱한 체구의 할아버지, 여덟마리 순록이 끄는 썰매를 타고 와서 굴뚝을 타고 내려와서 우리에게 선물을, 
김혜리의 #조용한생활 22년 10월호 #이진숙 @stilllife.audio_magazine
우연히 오늘의 조식을 준비하며 들은 성 니콜라오스에 관한 이야기. 외모에 관한 묘사에 없었던 빨간색 옷은 훗날 코카콜라 마케팅팀에서 만들어낸 것이라고, 
오늘의 조식은 메리 크리스마스 에디션 갈레뜨,
-달군 팬에 올리브오일, 마늘과 양파를 볶아서 한쪽에 덜어둔다. 
-같은 팬에 올리브오일, 시금치를 넣고 소금소금, 후추후추, 마찬가지 방법으로 세상에서 제일 예쁜 당근도 굽는다. 베이컨과 토마토도 준비한다. 
-팬에 올리브오일 조금, 시판 크레페를 올린 뒤 계란 한 알, 준비해 둔 마늘과 양파를 계란 가장자리에 올리고 네 면을 접는다. 
-접시에 옮긴 후 준비해둔 시금치, 당근, 토마토, 베이컨을 올린다. 후추후추, 파마산치즈를 듬뿍 #갈레뜨

_en.title: Christmas Galette
_en.intro:
20221225, #breakfastdiary 634, -7°C/clear, 26min/exercise
A Visit from St. Nicholas, the 1822 poem by Clement Moore, describes his appearance: a rosy-faced, white-bearded, round old man who rides in on a sleigh pulled by eight reindeer and comes down the chimney to bring us gifts.
Kim Hye-ri's #thequietlife, October 2022 issue, #leejinsook @stilllife.audio_magazine
A story about St. Nicholas I happened to hear while making today's breakfast. Apparently the red suit — nowhere in that original description — was invented later by Coca-Cola's marketing team.
Today's breakfast is a Merry Christmas edition galette.
1. In a hot pan with olive oil, sauté garlic and onion, then set aside.
2. In the same pan with olive oil, cook the spinach with a little salt and pepper, and sear the prettiest carrots in the world the same way. Prep the bacon and tomato too.
3. With a touch of olive oil in the pan, lay down a store-bought crepe, crack an egg onto it, place the reserved garlic and onion around the edge of the egg, and fold in all four sides.
4. Move it to a plate and top with the prepared spinach, carrot, tomato, and bacon. Finish with pepper and a generous helping of parmesan. #galette

_en.title: Falafel Salad
_en.intro:
20221222, #breakfastdiary 631, -9°C/mostly clear
People who once immersed themselves in the idea of "experience" are now bringing their old imaginings to life. Honey named after a city, a neighborhood — how appealing is that to a traveler?
Does the honey taste different from neighborhood to neighborhood, you ask? Absolutely — because the flowers blooming there differ too. Eunpyeong-gu in Seoul has a grove of Korean mountain ash trees, so the honey there carries the scent of their blossoms. Over in Yeouido, the honey smells of cherry blossoms.
Honey made in the city is, in itself, a story. Even the most expensive honey in France, they say, comes from Paris. Hearing that, I thought, "we could do that too." People who love a good story really do collect honey from each different neighborhood.
Park Jin, Urban Bees: Raising Bees on City Rooftops, Growing a Sweet Ecosystem @longblack.co

같은 브랜드의 맥주와 무알콜 맥주를 놓고 시음한 적이 있었는데 무알콜맥주의 향이 더 짙었다. 맥주가 아닌 녀석이 진짜 맥주인양 가장하기 위해서였을 터, 세상 모든 가짜는 다 그렇다. 
달군 팬에 올리브오일, 허브, 소금, 후추후추 느타리버섯을 굽는다. 
끓는 물에 꼰낄리에를 삶고 면수를 덜어낸 뒤 불을 줄인 뒤 페스토를 적당히 넣어 뒤섞뒤섞, 접시로 옮기고 느타리버섯, 페코리노 치즈 갉갉갉, #꼰낄리에페스토파스타

같은 브랜드의 맥주와 무알콜 맥주를 놓고 시음한 적이 있었는데 무알콜맥주의 향이 더 짙었다. 맥주가 아닌 녀석이 진짜 맥주인양 가장하기 위해서였을 터, 세상 모든 가짜는 다 그렇다. 

달군 팬에 올리브오일, 허브, 소금, 후추후추 느타리버섯을 굽는다. 
끓는 물에 꼰낄리에를 삶고 면수를 덜어낸 뒤 불을 줄인 뒤 페스토를 적당히 넣어 뒤섞뒤섞, 접시로 옮기고 느타리버섯, 페코리노 치즈 갉갉갉, #꼰낄리에페스토파스타

_en.title: Conchiglie Pesto Pasta with Oyster Mushrooms
_en.intro:
20221214, #breakfastdiary 625, -12°C/mostly clear, 11min/exercise
Doing my #yearendreview — my #drinkoftheyear is #nonalcoholic beer. I'm not much for soda, but whenever I craved a drink or just needed something to quench my thirst, non-alcoholic beers were always a great companion.
I once did a side-by-side tasting of a regular beer and its non-alcoholic version from the same brand, and the non-alcoholic one actually had the stronger aroma — probably trying that much harder to pass itself off as the real thing. That's how every fake in the world seems to work.
Sear the oyster mushrooms in a hot pan with olive oil, herbs, salt, and pepper.
Boil the conchiglie in water, reserve some pasta water, lower the heat, stir in a good amount of pesto, then plate it up with the oyster mushrooms and a generous grating of pecorino. #conchigliepestopasta

_en.title: Polenta with Oyster Mushrooms
_en.intro:
20221213, #breakfastdiary 624, 0°C/mostly cloudy, 11min/exercise
Both in Italy and here in Korea, in hard times people boiled up corn porridge to eat — that's polenta. Interestingly, in southern Italy it was also used as a mocking term for northerners.
The ratio of polenta to water is 1:4. Add salt and olive oil to boiling water, then stir in the polenta little by little. Add a generous handful of parmesan and turn off the heat.
Top with oyster mushrooms sautéed in olive oil, salt, pepper, and herbs, then finish with a generous grating of parmesan. #polenta
Next time, I'll try slicing the parmesan thin instead of grating it.

title: 챗지피티 딸기오픈샌드위치 모닝루틴
intro:
20221212, #조식다이어리 623, -4도/흐림, 11분/운동
인간의 언어에 인간처럼 반응하고 글을 쏟아내는 기계를 대하고 있자니, 자명한 지식을 습득하기 위해 10여년을 허비하는 교육체계가 얼마나 허망한지 더욱 절실하게 다가온다. 답을 내는 것은 이제 기계의 몫이 돼가고 있다. 제대로 질문하고 문제화하는 능력을 기르는 게 더욱 중요해졌다. 정말이지 그저 수사가 아니라 실질적으로, 질문하는 능력이 인간 조건의 근간이 되고 있다.
(김진화, 챗봇이 일깨워 준 인간의 조건)
#챗지피티 #ChatGPT 얘기다. 아직 한글 서비스 수준은 아쉽지만, 어쩐지 인간 같다는 느낌을 주었는데 그 가운데 하나는 답변 확인을 위해 다시 물으면 그게 아니라 이거야 혹은 맞아 하면서 주는 피드백이었다. 
질문하는 능력 뿐만 아니라 적절한 피드백 능력이야 말로 인간의 기본 조건 아닐까하는 생각이 들면서 챗지피티 앞에서 부끄러운 생각이, 
달군 팬, 사워도우 앞뒤로 올리브오일을 두르고 바삭하게 굽는다. 
리코타치즈를 바르고 딸기를 반으로 썰어 예쁘게 올린다. #딸기오픈샌드위치

_en.title: Strawberry Open Sandwich
_en.intro:
20221212, #breakfastdiary 623, -4°C/cloudy, 11min/exercise
Facing a machine that responds to human language and pours out text almost like a person, the emptiness of an education system that wastes ten-plus years teaching self-evident knowledge hits home even harder. Producing answers is increasingly becoming the machine's job. What matters more now is cultivating the ability to ask the right questions and frame the right problems. Truly, not just as a rhetorical flourish but in practical terms, the ability to ask questions is becoming the foundation of the human condition.
(Kim Jin-hwa, What the Chatbot Taught Us About Being Human)
This is about #chatgpt #ChatGPT. Its Korean-language service still leaves something to be desired, but it somehow felt oddly human — one reason being that when I asked it to double-check an answer, it would come back with feedback like "no, actually it's this" or "yes, that's right."
It struck me that not just the ability to ask questions, but the ability to give proper feedback, might really be a basic condition of being human — and that made me feel a bit humbled in front of ChatGPT.
In a hot pan, toast sourdough on both sides in olive oil until crisp.
Spread on ricotta cheese and arrange halved strawberries neatly on top. #strawberryopensandwich

title: 모닝루틴 덮밥 병아리콩
intro:
20221206, #조식다이어리 616, -3도/대체로흐림, 21분/운동
신형철 선생의 책을 가까이 두고 매일 조금씩 읽고 있다. 
영혼은 비행기처럼 빨리 날 수 없다는 것을 인디언에 관해 쓴 어떤 책에서 읽은 적이 있다. 그래서 사람들은 비행 기를 타고 여행할 때 영혼을 잃어버리고 영혼이 없는 채 로 목적지에 도착한다. 심지어는 시베리아 열차도 영혼이 나는 것보다 빨리 간다. 나는 처음 유럽에 올 때 시베리아 기차를 타고 오면서 내 영혼을 잃어버렸다. (…) 그 다음에 나는 몇 번 비행기를 타고 오고 가고 했는데 도무지 내 영혼이 어디에 있는지를 알 수 없었다. 어찌 되었든 그것이 여행자들은 왜 모두 영혼이 없는지에 대한 이유가 된다.
(신형철, 슬픔을 공부하는 슬픔) 
불린 병아리콩을 잘 삶아서 올리브오일, 참깨, 레몬주스, 다진 마늘, 소금, 후추를 넣고 간다. 간다. 간다. 타임과 파프리카 분말, 요거트를 넣으면 더욱 그럴싸한 후무스가 된다.

_en.title: Homemade Hummus
_en.intro:
20221206, #breakfastdiary 616, -3°C/mostly cloudy, 21min/exercise
I keep a book by Shin Hyung-cheol close at hand and read a little of it every day.
I once read, in a book about Native Americans, that the soul cannot fly as fast as an airplane. So when people travel by plane, they lose their soul along the way and arrive at their destination soulless. Even the Trans-Siberian train travels faster than a soul can fly. When I first came to Europe, I lost my soul somewhere along that train ride. (…) After that, I flew back and forth by plane several times, and I could never quite tell where my soul was. That, in any case, is the reason travelers are all soulless.
(Shin Hyung-cheol, The Sorrow of Studying Sorrow)
Boil well-soaked chickpeas, then blend them with olive oil, sesame seeds, lemon juice, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Blend, blend, blend. Add thyme, paprika powder, and yogurt, and it turns into a proper-tasting hummus.

_en.title: Tomato Spinach Chickpea Salad Morning Routine Rice Bowl
_en.intro:
20221204 #breakfastdiary 614, -6°C/mostly cloudy, 27 min/workout
The World Cup is in full swing. I tend to avoid watching live, since our team usually seems to win more often when I'm not watching. 
One photo of the German national team caught my eye. Before their match, the players reportedly covered their mouths with their hands in protest of FIFA banning the rainbow 'One Love' armband, which stands for LGBTQ+ rights and against discrimination. It really showcased how seriously Germany takes standing against discrimination as a core social value. 
In a heated pan with olive oil, I sear cherry tomatoes, then add in the prettiest spinach in the world and blanch it briefly. Salt, salt, pepper, pepper, then in go the pre-boiled chickpeas for a little more blanching. Move it all to a plate and finish with vinaigrette dressing. #tomatospinachchickpeasalad 
A recipe by @vo.s_kitchen.

_en.intro:

Flipping through the newspaper, my eyes land on a review of Professor Jeong Su-il's memoir, 'A Man of His Times, Following His Calling.' 앱을 활용해 돈을 버는 '앱테크' 언급량은 2019년 1분기 대비 2022년 4~5월에 4.7배 증가했다. 
출석체크, 퀴즈 등의 간단한 미션을 수행하거나 광고를 시청하고 소소한 적립 포인트를 모으는 방식으로, 기업은 비교적 적은 비용으로 소비자에게 메시지를 전달할 수 있고 사람들은 큰 노력 없이 포인트를 쌓을 수 있다.
하루에 수십 번씩 휴대폰 들여다보는 시간을 할애해 적은 노력으로 현금화하기 편리한 적립금을 쌓는 일종의 게임이다. 돈을 많이 벌겠다는 목적보다는 일상의 소소한 재미와 함께 포인트가 조금씩 쌓이는 기쁨을 얻을 수 있다.
퍼블리 @publy.co , 2023 마케터를 위한 트렌드 노트

굴소스1, 간장3, 꿀1, 물을 적당히 부어 드레싱을 만들어 팬에 붓고 졸인다. 플레이팅하고 쪽파를 송송 썰어 #가지덮밥

_en.title: Eggplant Rice Bowl Morning Routine Rice Bowl
_en.intro:
20221129 #breakfastdiary 610, 8°C/cloudy, 16 min/workout
Mentions of 'app-tech' — making money through apps — rose 4.7 times between Q1 2019 and April–May 2022. 
By completing simple missions like daily check-ins or quizzes, or watching ads, people rack up small reward points; companies get to deliver their message to consumers at relatively low cost, and people can pile up points without much effort. 
It's a kind of game where you spend the time you'd spend glancing at your phone dozens of times a day anyway, and turn it into easily cashable rewards with minimal effort. The point isn't so much making a lot of money as the small daily fun of watching the points slowly add up. 
Publly @publy.co, 2023 Trend Notes for Marketers 
I wonder if the resurgence of these old-school check-in style events reflects a reality where the things we actually want feel completely out of reach — so if that's too far off, we settle for this instead. Kind of like an eggplant rice bowl made to look like grilled eel. 
Peel the eggplant with a vegetable peeler, slice it thin, and steam it. Sear both sides in a hot, oiled pan. 
Make a sauce with 1 part oyster sauce, 3 parts soy sauce, 1 part honey and a splash of water, pour it into the pan, and let it reduce. Plate it up and sprinkle with sliced scallions. #eggplantricebowl

title: 그남자네집 모닝루틴 굴
intro:

신형철 선생의 책을 가까이 두고 매일 조금씩 읽고 있다. 책에 등장하는 박완서 선생의 #그남자네집 가운데 한 대목이다. 
쌍쌍이 붙어 앉아 서로를 진하게 애무하고 있는 젊은이들에게 늙은이 하나가 들어가든 나가든 아랑곳없으려만 나는 마치 그들이 그 옛날의 내 외설스러운 순결주의를 비웃기라도 하는 것처럼 뒤꼭지가 머쓱했다. 온 세상이 저 애들 놀아나라고 깔아놓은 멍석인데 나는 어디로 가야 하나.
그래, 실칫 젊음을 낭비하려무나. 넘칠 때 낭비하는 건 죄가 아니라 미덕이다. 낭비하지 못하고 아껴둔다고 그게 영원히 네 소유가 되는 건 아니란다. 나는 젊은이들한테 빼지 리는 마음을 겨우 이렇게 다독거렸다. 
(신형철, 슬픔을 공부하는 슬픔)
이모가 보내주신 김장 김치에 굴을 곁들여 먹었다. 
아마 이모나 어머니 세대 이후엔 김장을 담그는 일도 눈에 띄게 줄어들 것이다. 묻지도 않고 김장김치를 보낸 이모를 탓하며 어머니에게 불만을 토로했던 일을 후회하는 중이다.

_en.title: That Man's House Morning Routine Oysters
_en.intro:
20221127 #breakfastdiary 608, 1°C/clear
I keep Shin Hyung-cheol's book close by and read a little every day. Here's a passage from Park Wan-suh's #thatmanshouse, quoted in it. 
'To the young couples sitting pair by pair, wrapped up in each other, it probably wouldn't matter whether some old person walked in or out. Yet I felt my neck go hot with embarrassment, as if they were mocking my own old-fashioned, prudish sense of purity from years ago. The whole world has laid out this mat for them to play on — so where am I supposed to go? 
Well then, go ahead and waste your youth. Wasting it while you have plenty isn't a sin, it's a virtue. Holding back and saving it up doesn't mean it'll stay yours forever. That's how I quietly consoled the part of me that felt left out of the young people's world.' 
(Shin Hyung-cheol, Sorrow Studying Sorrow)
I had oysters alongside the kimjang kimchi my aunt sent me. 
I suspect that after my aunt's and mother's generation, the tradition of making kimjang kimchi will keep visibly fading. I'm regretting having complained to my mom about my aunt sending kimchi without even asking first.

intro:

보통의 빵집에서는 마감 시간이 되면 세일을 해요. 당일 생산한 빵은 오늘이 지나면 상품 가치가 떨어지기 때문이죠. 어차피 버려질 거라면 할인을 해서라도 파는 편이 나은 선택이에요. 밤의 빵집은 이렇게 다른 베이커리에서 버려질지도 모르는 빵을 할인된 가격에 사서, 정가에 판매해요. 그것도 하나의 빵집이 아니라 여러 빵집에서요. 그래서 영업 시간도 보통의 베이커리가 영업을 마무리하는 시간에 시작하는 거예요.
(중략) 
밤의 빵집은 노숙인의 자립을 돕는 잡지인 ‘빅이슈’에서 운영해요. 노숙인의 자립과 식량 낭비라는 사회적 문제를 동시에 해결하기 위해 밤의 빵집을 기획한 거죠. 그래서 각 빵집을 돌면서 빵을 할인된 가격으로 사오는 역할을 노숙자가 담당해요. 이런 철학까지 담겨 있으니 빵집도, 손님도 돈쭐을 내주며 따뜻한 응원을 보낼 수 밖에요.
씨티호퍼스 @cityhoppers 버려진 재료를 술로 살려내는, 세계 최초의 ‘재활용 양조장’
도쿄에 있다는 밤의 빵집 이야기, 혹시 냉장고에 버려지는 식재료는 없는지 살핀다. 
(유통기한이 지난) 두부 한 모를 썰어 들기름 두른 팬에 앞뒤로 굽는다. 간장, 참깨, 들기름, 다진 깻잎 드레싱을 얹는다.

_en.title: Morning Routine Grilled Tofu Perilla Oil
_en.intro:
20221125 #breakfastdiary 606, 5°C/occasionally cloudy
Most bakeries put their bread on sale right around closing time. Bread baked that day loses its value as merchandise once the day is over, so if it's going to be thrown out anyway, selling it at a discount is the better option. The Night Bakery buys up bread that other bakeries might otherwise toss out, at a discounted price, and resells it at full price — and not from just one bakery, but many. That's why its hours start right around when regular bakeries are closing up. 
(omitted) 
The Night Bakery is run by The Big Issue, a magazine that helps homeless people become self-reliant. It was designed to tackle both homeless self-sufficiency and food waste at the same time. Homeless workers are the ones who go around buying up the discounted bread from each bakery. With a philosophy like that behind it, both the bakery and the customers can't help but want to cheer it on warmly. 
Cityhoppers @cityhoppers, 'The World's First Recycling Brewery,' turning discarded ingredients into alcohol 
The story of Tokyo's Night Bakery makes me check my own fridge for any ingredients about to go to waste. 
I slice up a block of tofu (just past its use-by date) and sear it on both sides in a pan with perilla oil. Top it with a dressing of soy sauce, sesame seeds, perilla oil, and chopped perilla leaves.

생물학적인 죽음이 될 수도 있고, 누군가와의 헤어짐이 될 수도 있죠. 안 친했던 동료가 이직으로 책상을 빼는 날이었어요. 짐이 많길래, 같이 들어주는데 ‘언제 차 한잔 하자’ 하더라고요. 저는 차마 그 말을 하진 못했어요. 너무 평범한 말이라서. 그리고 알았죠. 우리가 따로 연락해서 만날 관계가 아니란걸. 그런데 그 말이 무성의하다고 생각하지 않았어요. 그 상황에서 할 수 있는 최선의 말이라고 생각했거든요.
빤한 말이지만 이게 이 사람이 이 상황에서 내보일 수 있는 최선의 다정이라고 생각하면 애틋해져요. 이렇게 일상적인 말도 누군가를 떠올리면 얼굴과 동시에 남아 있는데, 오늘 내가 하는 말이 누군가에게 남기는 유언이 될 수 있다고 생각하면 말 한마디 한마디가 허투루 나가지는 않는 것 같아요.
박준, 어떤 말들은 죽지 않고, 사람 마음 속에 오래 살아남는다 @longblack.co

_en.title: Combination Salad Morning Routine Broccoli
_en.intro:
20221124 #breakfastdiary 605, 3°C/cloudy, 23 min/workout
It could be a biological death, or it could be a parting from someone. It was the day a coworker I wasn't especially close to was clearing out their desk after changing jobs. They had a lot of stuff, so I helped carry it, and they said, 'Let's grab coffee sometime.' I couldn't quite bring myself to say it back — it felt too ordinary a thing to say. And that's when I realized we weren't the kind of people who'd actually reach out and meet up separately. But I didn't think the remark was insincere. I think it was the best thing that person could offer in that moment. 
It's a cliché, but when you think of it as the best warmth a person can show in that situation, it becomes touching. Even an everyday phrase like that stays with someone's face in your memory — so when I think that the words I say today could become the last words I leave with someone, I find myself not wanting to let a single word go to waste. 
Park Jun, 'Some Words Never Die, They Live On for a Long Time in a Person's Heart,' @longblack.co 
A line worth chewing on again: the words I say today could be the last words I leave with someone. 
Broccoli, cauliflower, sweet potato, egg, and tomato with pan-seared tofu tenders, crushed walnuts, and an elegant vinaigrette dressing. #combinationsalad

_en.title: Avocado-Topped Sweet Potato Toast Morning Routine Avocado
_en.intro:
20221122 #breakfastdiary 603, 5°C/cloudy, 19 min/workout
I keep Shin Hyung-cheol's book close by and read a little every day. 
Let me talk about violence again. I once suggested that the scope of the word 'violence' should probably be widened as much as possible, and tried to define it broadly like this: 'Violence is any attitude that finds satisfaction in giving up the effort to be as sensitive as possible to the truth of a person or an event.' What I wanted to say is that the moment we could be more sensitive but choose not to be, potential — or actual — violence toward another person begins. Of course that's not the end of it; I've found myself thinking about violence often ever since. 
Shin Hyung-cheol, Sorrow Studying Sorrow 
Slice a sweet potato lengthwise and sear it on both sides in an oiled pan. 
Mash half an avocado with salt, pepper and lime juice, then spoon it over the sweet potato. Finish with pecorino cheese, red pepper flakes and honey. #avocadotoppedsweetpotatotoast

_en.title: Sweet Potato with Greek Yogurt Morning Routine Sweet Potato
_en.intro:
20221120 #breakfastdiary 601, 10°C/occasionally cloudy, 23 min/workout
Cut the prettiest sweet potato in the world into bite-sized pieces and toss with potato starch, paprika, herbs, salt, pepper, and olive oil, then roast at 210°C for 30 minutes. 
Stir lemon juice, minced garlic, honey and pecorino cheese into Greek yogurt to make a dressing. 
Spread the dressing on the bottom of the plate, then scatter the roasted sweet potato, perilla leaves, and walnuts on top. #sweetpotatowithgreekyogurt 
I only added the tiniest bit of minced garlic, but the smell really lingers. Whew~ 🌬️

_en.title: The Taste of Adulthood Eggplant Rice Bowl Morning Routine
_en.intro:
20221119 #breakfastdiary 600, 10°C/mostly cloudy
Maybe the moment you learn to appreciate the taste of eggplant is the moment you actually become an adult? #tasteofadulthood, something kids just don't get. 
Mix soy sauce, sugar, cooking wine, water and Yondu (a Korean seasoning sauce) in equal parts. Add a little scallion too. 
Score the eggplant and open it up, then grill it while brushing on the sauce evenly. 
Lay it over rice and finish with sesame oil, sesame seeds and perilla leaves. #eggplantricebowl

_en.title: Morning Routine Udon Goraesa
_en.intro:
20221118 #breakfastdiary 599, 4°C/mostly clear
May my dream become a clear wind
Han Yong-un, My Dream
This year's 2023 CSAT handwriting-verification phrase — since there isn't much else to say about today's breakfast, I looked up the phrases used across the years: 
Dreaming of soaring into the wide sky
Lee Hae-in, Little Song 2 (2022)
Among the countless people in this world, you are the one
Na Tae-ju, Walking the Country Path (2021)
One star among so many, so clear and bright
Park Du-jin, Lying in a Field of Stars (2020)
I have never seen anyone as lovely as you
Kim Nam-jo, A Letter (2019)
We have been given a great sea and a wide sky
Kim Young-nang, Let's Go to the Sea (2018)
My heart, grown up from this soil, the pale blue of the sky
Jeong Ji-yong, Nostalgia (2017)
Filling my heart with breadth and depth
Ju Yo-han, Sing, Young Ones (2016)
A clear day when even the sunlight gathers into soft round shapes
Mun Tae-jun, The Stone's Boat (2015)
Shall I light up my eyes like a lantern of flowers
Park Jeong-man, A Little Love Song (2014)
Dyeing everything with sparkling, clear sunlight
Jeong Han-mo, In Autumn (2013)
The real reason I love you
Hwang Dong-gyu, A Happy Letter (2012)
Every day made new, growing deeper and wider
Jeong Chae-bong, First Heart (2011)
Quiet and gentle like a clear river
Yu An-jin, Dreaming of a Deep Friendship (2010)
On this hill where so much starlight falls
Yun Dong-ju, Counting the Stars at Night (2009)
A clear river flowing across my palm
Yun Dong-ju, A Boy (2008)
Toward the eastern edge of the wide field
Jeong Ji-yong, Nostalgia (2007)
My heart, grown up from this soil, the blue of the sky
Jeong Ji-yong, Nostalgia (2006)
Here's hoping everyone gets the result they're after. 
Udon made with fish-cake noodles from Goraesa. 
Instead of the egg block that came with it, I added a real egg — probably not the reason, but cooked exactly by the recipe, it turned out a bit salty.

title: 대파크림치즈베이글 모닝루틴 베이글
intro:
20221116, #조식다이어리 598, 4도/대체로맑음, 16분/운동
한잔의 커피가 소중한 법이다. 이는 모든 기호품의 특징이기도 한데, 그것은 한순간, 한번, 한잔, 한 모금에 특별한 ‘존재적 의미’를 부여하며 즐기기 때문이다. 그것을 즐기는 순간에 다른 모든 것들은 존재 의미 영역 밖으로 퇴출당한다.
김용석, 커피: 아주 특별한 기호품
커피, 기호품을 넘어 필수품, 각성과 중독 사이 어딘가, 그리고 커피엔 베이글, 
대파를 송송송송송송 썰고 꿀 조금, 크림치즈를 넣은 뒤 쒜낏, 팬에 데운 베이글에 듬뿍 바른다 #대파크림치즈베이글

우리는 외부인에게 향수에 대한 의견을 묻지 않습니다. 나는 창조가 전제정치이지 민주주의가 아니라고 굳게 믿습니다. 특히 향수는 사람들에게 어떻게 생각하는지 묻는 게, 더더욱 이상적이지 않아요. 그 말에 과도하게 영향을 받아 개성이 희석되고, 결과적으로 대중 제품이 되기 때문이죠.

_en.title: Le Labo Perilla Oil Buckwheat Noodles Morning Routine
_en.intro:
20221115 #breakfastdiary 597, 3°C/mostly clear, 16 min/workout
'We don't ask outsiders for their opinion on fragrance. I firmly believe creation is a dictatorship, not a democracy. Asking people what they think, especially about fragrance, is even less ideal — you end up overly influenced by that feedback, your individuality gets diluted, and you end up with just another mass-market product.' 
Eddie Roschi, from a 2018 interview with Lifestyle Asia, @longblack.co 
#lelabo co-founder Eddie Roschi's words: creation is a dictatorship. Hmm, I'm more inclined to agree with Jobs' line that good artists copy, great artists steal. 
Boil buckwheat noodles, pouring in cold water now and then, then scoop them out and rinse in cold water. 
For the dressing: 2 parts Yondu, 2 parts water, 1 part sugar, topped with ground perilla seed, perilla leaves and gim (dried seaweed), finished with a good drizzle of perilla oil. #perillaoilbuckwheatnoodles 
Not my own recipe, of course.

title: 아치니디페페수프 양파 당근
intro:
20221114, #조식다이어리 596, 8도/흐림, 16분/운동
그러니까 아치니 디 페페는 작은 구슬 모양의 파스타다. 이탈리아에선 웨딩 수프로 나온다고 하니 마치 잔치국수 같은 것이 아닐까 싶다. 
작다고 우습게 볼 것은 아닌 것이 파스타이므로 익는데 그만큼의 시간이 걸린다. 충분히 삶을 시간이 없어 오늘 아침엔 알 덴테로(a.k.a. 설익은 채로)  먹었다. 
달군 팬에 올리브오일, 다진 마늘, 양파, 당근을 데친다. 각종 허브를 적당히 추가한다. 
물에 야채 스톡을 풀어서 넣고 아치니 디 페페를 넣은 뒤 삶는다. 익을 때쯤 완두콩을 넣고 접시로 옮긴 뒤 파마산 치즈 #아치니디페페수프
